Class Radio<T>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.AbstractPanelElement
com.trevlar.menukit.api.element.Radio<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value type of this Radio and its group
All Implemented Interfaces:
PanelElement
public class Radio<T> extends AbstractPanelElement
One choice of a single-selection set: a square with a dot when its value is the RadioGroup's selection, and a label beside it. 
RadioGroup<Mode> mode = RadioGroup.state(() -> config.mode, m -> config.mode = m);
Radio.builder(mode, Mode.FAST).label(Component.literal("Fast")).build();

The Radio stores nothing: it asks the group, which asks the consumer, every frame. A click anywhere on it (square or label) selects its value, with vanilla's click sound; Tab focuses it and Enter or Space selects it; the narrator reads its label and whether it is selected.

Sizes itself from its label, as Checkbox does, and wraps it the same way when the panel is narrower.

      public int extraLayoutHeight()
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement

    • isInteractive

      public boolean isInteractive()
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Whether this element handles pointer input, so a point on it is a solid claim on a transparent panel. Controls return true; render-only decorations keep the false default, so they never eat a click they do nothing with.

    • render

      public void render(RenderContext ctx)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      Renders this element at (ctx.originX() + getChildX(), ctx.originY() + getChildY()). When ctx.disabled() is true, an element draws its disabled look.

    • mouseClicked

      public boolean mouseClicked(InputContext in, int button)
      Description copied from interface: PanelElement
      A mouse click on this element (the dispatcher hit-tested first). Returns true if consumed, stopping dispatch to other elements, slots and vanilla. button is GLFW's (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle). Default: false.
